subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity — Pricing & sizing follow-up (FinTechX)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@fintechx.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated Capacity — Pricing & sizing follow-up

Thanks again for the time today, Sarah — great conversation. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated and put together an indicative pricing sheet: 

Summary of what I heard from the call:
- Baseline tokens: ~250M tokens/month (steady-state)
- Peak tokens: up to ~1.2B tokens in high months
- Typical interaction: chat-style sessions, ~40 concurrent active sessions at peak
- Average observed sequence: prompt ~120 tokens, completion ~220 tokens (avg ~340 tokens)
- Latency SLO target: 95th percentile streaming <300ms for short responses; willing to accept slightly higher for long completion streaming

Questions / clarifications we need to finalize sizing and pricing: 
1) GPU preference: you mentioned A100. Are you open to H100 for higher single-stream throughput if we can show cost parity?
2) Reserved capacity target: do you want a strict reserved commit (e.g., 4 GPUs) or a blended model (reserved + burst)?
3) Throughput target: can you confirm the target tokens/sec peak requirement (tokens/sec or concurrent sessions works) — we estimated ~3k tokens/sec based on the numbers above but want your confirmation.
4) Sequence worst-case: is 512 tokens the appropriate worst-case sequence length to size KV cache/latency?
5) Budget target: you mentioned wanting to get to roughly $/1M tokens in the low-to-mid range — can you confirm a target range (e.g., $800–$1,200 / 1M tokens)?

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben (SE) will run a quick sizing pass with the numbers above and propose 2 SKU options (A100-based and H100-based) with estimated reserved capacity and indicative $/1M token economics.
- I’ll circulate an indicative pricing PDF + deployment MAP for procurement to review (attached).
- If those look reasonable, we can lock a time this week to review sizing and procurement timeline (Calendly link below).

Thanks — I’ll wait for your confirmation on the 5 bullets so Ben can finalize a recommendation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing summary), MAP_deployment_plan.xlsx (deployment milestone plan)

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechx.com
Date: 2026-03-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity — Pricing & sizing follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the succinct recap. Below are answers inline / clarified: 

1) GPU preference: A100 is our current preference because our infra team already has experience with them. That said, we are open to H100 if the TCO works out; show us both options.

2) Reserved capacity: Procurement leans towards a reserved commit for predictable budgeting. Thinking 4 GPUs to start, with ability to add in quarter 2. We’re OK with a reserved + burst bucket for unexpected spikes.

3) Throughput: Your 3k tokens/sec estimate aligns with our initial modeling. To be concrete: peak sustained tokens/sec target ~3k, with short spikes up to ~4.5k for a few minutes during market opens.

4) Sequence worst-case: yes — 512 tokens is a safe worst-case for sizing. Average will be ~340 tokens as you noted.

5) Budget target: Procurement would like to see $/1M tokens in the $900–$1,100 range for a committed Reserved CAPEX/commit. If it’s outside that range please flag the assumptions that drive the delta. Note — we may have some flexibility on committed term in exchange for better unit economics (12–24 month commit).

Procurement timeline: our procurement team can sign off within 3–4 weeks after final pricing/contract language is reviewed. We’ll need a standard SOC2 + data isolation language (we discussed VPC/private deployment options).

Happy to hop on a 30-min sizing call with Ben.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Head of AI Platform | FinTechX
sarah.connors@fintechx.com
+1 (646) 555-2210

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@fintechx.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity — Pricing & sizing follow-up

Thanks — great inputs, Sarah. Quick SE sizing notes / assumptions so Marissa can capture in the pricing doc: 

- Assumptions: avg seq 340 tokens, worst-case 512 tokens; batch size 8 for throughput; KV cache hit rate assumed 20% for persistent chat flows.
- GPU sizing: rough rule-of-thumb: 1x H100 ~ 1.8–2x an A100 for single-stream latency/throughput in our runtime (depends on quantization/sequence length).
- If they commit to 4x GPUs:
  - Option A (4x A100): estimated sustained throughput ~3k tokens/sec (meets stated target) with headroom for short bursts.
  - Option B (2x H100): estimated sustained throughput ~3.6k tokens/sec (better burst handling and lower p95 latency under load).
- Ops notes: for predictable latency and KV cache sizing, we should recommend: 4x A100 reserved + 1–2 GPU burst pool OR 2x H100 reserved + 1 H100 burst depending on preference.

Indicative unit economics (very high level):
- For committed Reserved model (4 GPU commit, 12–24 month): we can get into the ~$850–$1,050 per 1M tokens envelope depending on utilization and burst configuration.
- If they pick H100 reserved, unit $/1M tokens trends lower at higher utilization but has higher fixed commit cost.

I’ll build two simple SKU lines (A100 path, H100 path) with assumptions called out (seq length, concurrency, KV hit, utilization %) and hand back to Marissa to include in the deck.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
